text:
Maria: Quick sync: thinking about moving a small, deterministic policy evaluator into a sidecar to speed hot-path routing decisions. Wanted to capture tradeoffs here.
Kishore: Can you define "small"? What's the exact subset of policy we push to sidecars?
Maria: Small = ~10-20 predicates, no heavy arithmetic, no external price feeds. Focus: region affinity, latency thresholds, tenant-tier overrides, simple preemptive flags.
Sam: Observed 95/99 path regressions from runtime RPCs during bursts. Sidecar local eval would shave ~2-8ms on critical path. Worth exploring.
Elaine: Main concerns: staleness, extra rollout complexity, and that eval divergence could cause capacity imbalances.
Maria: Proposal: authoritative policies live in control plane. We ship signed incremental deltas to sidecars. Sidecar runs "fast-eval" grammar with strict semantics. If sidecar can't decide, it falls back to control plane.
Kishore: How do we handle deltas? streaming vs periodic? Do we need CRDTs to support out-of-order apply?
Sam: Keep it simple: versioned deltas + monotonic version number. Apply only when version == expected_next. If mismatch, sidecar fetches full snapshot. No need for CRDT complexity for MVP.
Elaine: Also add a TTL on versions. If version_age > t, sidecar enters conservative mode and adds penalty to its preferences or routes to best-effort pool.
Maria: Agreed. Conservative defaults: prefer lowest-latency shard, avoid preemptive decisions unless explicitly allowed.
Kishore: We must define the fast-eval grammar. Suggest primitives: equality (region == X), numeric compare (latency_p99 < N), set membership (tenant_flag in [A,B]), and a simple priority bucket output. No maps, no joins, no expensive functions.
Sam: Sidecar should not compute cost-sensitive tradeoffs that need price feeds or FX. Sidecar can emit a "cost_hint: low/neutral/high" but final cost-aware routing decisions are control-plane-only.
Elaine: Telemetry: tag every trace with policy.eval=sidecar|controlplane and policy.version. We should also emit a metric for sidecar_decision_ratio and sidecar_stale_count.
Maria: Failure modes to consider: 1) control plane outage -> sidecars still make decisions (OK if conservative); 2) sidecar stuck on old version -> capacity pressure; 3) slow apply path causing brief inconsistency.
Sam: For (2), add an emergency kill-switch in runtime and an admin endpoint on sidecar to force stale-mode or pull snapshot. Also expose a rolling kill switch from control plane via feature flag.
Kishore: How about determinism testing? Sidecar vs control-plane same input must yield identical result for the supported grammar. Need fuzz tests and golden inputs.
Elaine: Tests: - deterministic fuzzing across grammar - network partition chaos (control-plane unreachable) - perf tests target: sidecar eval P50 < 100us and P99 < 1ms - rollout canary in low-traffic region.
Maria: Rollout plan draft: (1) define grammar + schema and signature format (2) implement sidecar SDK + sync (3) read-mirror mode in runtime (no writes) to collect diffs (4) gated canary write with small tenant subset -> expand.
Sam: Also add a mirror-read run where runtime evaluates both sidecar and control-plane and logs mismatches for an initial period before enabling writes.
Kishore: Metrics to monitor: decision_mismatch_rate, sidecar_version_age_seconds, sidecar_evals_total, sidecar_fallbacks_total, capacity_pressure_by_tenant.
Elaine: Operational playbooks: steps for rollbacks, how to force global snapshot refresh, and how to evacuate sidecars if they cause pressure.
Maria: Action items: Kishore: draft grammar and versioning spec (EOW). Sam: prototype sync + telemetry tags (next sprint). Elaine: rollout checklist + chaos scenarios (next week).
deploy-bot: deploy request submitted by Maria for branch policy-sidecar-proto -> staging (CI: queued)
Maria: I'll write an RFC follow-up with these bullets. If anyone sees a missing failure mode or strong objection, call it out here. Thanks!
